trails.title: Trail ① The Night before the Gunshot

content.text: Darling, did you hear that? The sound of a match scraping against the box, igniting in a dark, silent alley ... and then, "BOOM!"
War, like an unstoppable train, hurtles down the track with its passengers, vanishing in the thick, black smoke.
In the train, the elderly tremble in the corner, and the infants babble dreaming ...
Ah, but the only young man aboard is filling coal into the furnace. Meanwhile, another train is hurtling down the same track, puffing the same black smoke ...
Alas. The two trains are destined to collide, in "a war to end all wars."
Who are the passengers on the other train?

branch.text: Pay close attention. You'll see the banner reaching out above their train, and the bloodstains on it.
Next, let's turn to where the train departed, to find the source of everything.
Rewind the clock to before the whistle blew, before the furnace ignited ...
And then, child, look somewhere far from here—in the Schönbrunn Palace, where the fine gentlemen of Austria-Hungary eagerly plan the extension of their national borders.
But the Habsburgs value their "honor" so much that first they must find themselves some excuse to cross that border.
Yet in another land, a humiliated people were gathering in secret. Their blood as hot as fire, ready to burn anyone and anywhere it was splattered.
Fate drove an open-topped car there, carrying an ill-fated couple. Their presence a crushing indignity that could not be endured.
An avenging bullet was sent to them as a gift from a luck-struck patriot.
In a moment, each party was granted their long-sought excuse. Boots had their excuse to kick down their doors, and guns their excuse to fire.
A yearning furnace at last had its reason to burn, to steam toward its final destination.
My dear, it's not a story of hatred or anger. The footprints were laid down before you ever stepped forward into them.
Fresh-faced boys traded books and toys for rifles, and poets were buried in trenches, musicians deafened by explosions and the howls of death.
But those war-starters? Those who doodled their ambitions on maps while supping their dessert, would lose nothing in their gamble.
The dew-fed river would still flow, and the facades of their great palaces would never be chipped or rocked by the guns they set off.
Nothing stains their hands, save the cream from their cakes.

content.text: Is there nothing we can do to stop all this?

branch.text: Perhaps ... We wait. Wait for a pouring rain to douse the fires, a flood that might sweep the armies, wagered like betting chips, from their maps.
Then perhaps that car will turn, and the fated dead will come back to life—But you know that will not be how the story ends.

items.text: With Hope Rekindled

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Burn these letters, Marcus.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Destroy them in accordance with the Field Mission Manual Article 341 so that no one else can read them.
Hofmann walks briskly, handing over the latest reviewed letter to her assistant.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ok, Madam Hofmann ... But shouldn't we reply to these messages from the Field squad?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Don't bother. The secret letters are sent to all active investigators above rank four.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The squad is like the watchers of the Critical Points. They collect and record every event different to the ones in history and report to the Foundation. These incidents will be the index for evaluating the stability of the current era.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: In other words, the more reports they send, the more unstable the era is.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: This keeps every field investigator up to date on the situation so they can plan their next move. In the past, we have seen too many tragedies caused by a lack of information.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: But now, our own task is more urgent.
Hofmann bites her lip, rushing Marcus around a corner.
Recent events have added a few more strands of white to her hair.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: "The Circle" publicly committed treason, Isolde and Heinrich disappeared, Kakania became wanted.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The Leopoldstadt riots and the march of the lower-class arcanists may be directly related to them.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Heinrich and Isolde's speech is like the spark that ignited the powder keg that is Vienna. The riots have been going on for days.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But ... Why was Ms. Kakania wanted?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: She didn't act out of line in the exhibition, and seemed totally unaware of the speech. All she had was the book which didn't belong to this era. Clearly, Heinrich didn't tell her a thing!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: It's because she is the known founder of "The Circle," and a middle class with no background.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: This is good news for us, Marcus. We can start with Kakania. They didn't protect her from being wanted, which means she hasn't been fully assimilated into this elite group of nobles.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: How typical of Manus Vindictae. We need to find her fast.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Luckily, the Spider Tail you put on her is reacting.
*crash*
Stones scrape over the top of her head.
The investigators turn back in shock.
The statue standing at the entrance to the Foundation's Vienna branch has just been shattered to pieces.
A hysterical laugh can be heard booming from the fourth-floor window.

items.speaker: Rioter
items.text: Hahahaha! Go to hell, you dirty, disgusting officials!

items.speaker: Rioter
items.text: For a kingdom of freedom!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: For a ... kingdom of freedom ...?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Shoot, they're attacking the Foundation branch?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Focus on what's important, Marcus! Someone's summoned a bunch of critters on Carinthian Street! They're coming this way!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: *coughing*
A strangely scented smoke spreads out over the street, making the already chaotic scene even more incomprehensible.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Something's wrong with this mist. Maybe the evaporation of the arcane potion. *cough* Devil's Shoestring, judging by the smell ... For better diffusivity?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Marcus, cover your mouth and nose. We'll enter the Foundation's branch when it clears up.
Hofmann pulls Marcus's hand, darting through the crowd at speed to avoid inhaling more of the unknown gas.
At last, they reach an area not yet engulfed by chaos.
For now, all that's left for them is to wait.
The unseasoned investigator stands stunned and uncharacteristically vacant in mind.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Marcus, are you ok? Did the mist get to you?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: No ...
Marcus pats her head, where a layer of cold sweat has formed.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Madam Hofmann, the terrorists and the people in the march, what they shouted, "for a kingdom of freedom" ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: That's-that's what Ms. Dittarsdorf said in the exhibit, and she quoted that from Dr. Kakania ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: And-and it was me ... I told that to Dr. Kakania! I told her about the island, I told her it's a place of freedom for arcanists!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: So-so I'm the one who caused this turmoil! I told them the secret of the Golden Isle and caused the chain reaction!
Hofmann seems to have neither words of comfort nor criticism planned. She bites her tongue in her mouth.
Marcus, meanwhile, collapses slowly to the ground as she holds her head.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I didn't listen to you ... I'm too reckless, I lack rational thinking, I'm unstable and out of control ... And the one thing I can control, my arcane skill, didn't help at all ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: You vouched for me and appointed me to the field mission from the headquarters, but I ...!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: ... Maybe it is like what you said.
Hofmann rubs her temples figuratively, ignoring the now-pale complexion of her subordinate.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Maybe you did play a role in this era, causing a butterfly effect in history ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: But trying to be responsible for everything beyond one's capability is a symbol of irrational hubris.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: First of all, creating chaos in this chaotic time is more than easy. Just look at all the frequent ethnic conflicts, assassinations, and espionage.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: If not "The Circle" and Isolde, the Manus will find themselves a different flashpoint.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: You never know how the leaked information will simmer. Its subsequent spread is uncontrollable, and remorse would be useless.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The thing is, everyone has their own ideas about that island. Your words just deepened their expectations.
Her cheeks finally regain some color.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: As for your self assessment ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: We have all heard it: humans are more rational and arcanists are more emotional.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: They're sensitive to the darkness in the world, so they can easily become absorbed in their own emotions and ignore reality.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: But if we put a human child in the position of an arcanist, who always takes on the world because of his uniqueness, who is never understood for his talents ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Maybe he too will become impulsive, sensitive, immature and unstable.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: And that's why it sometimes dawns on me that if we put an arcanist child in the position of a human being who receives enough love, education, and positive feedback ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: These "instabilities" might be controllable. At least enough to keep them from hurting themselves or others.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Madam Hofmann ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I took you away from the "Storm" in 1912. It's been a long time after that, so I know how precious it must be for you to return to 1914.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: And your urge to complete the mission, and go back to Romania.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: You're not an impulsive person, Marcus, you're just growing up.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: And you do need to grow.
Hofmann brings her hand to her mouth, coughing softly and hesitantly.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: As for appointing you, it was by my own will.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Because, the age of humans has come to an end.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The age of humans ... is ending?
Marcus staggers back to her feet.
Contrary to her expectations, Hofmann's expression is unchanged.
As if she is merely stating an established fact.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: If the eras keep on regressing, human technologies would fail to accumulate.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Meanwhile, arcane skills that depend largely on the individual's potential, will shine.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: In this war of reversals, futures, and time, it is you who will survive, not us. And that's why sooner or later, you'll have to go at it alone.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: This is the most rational assessment I can make for the continuation of civilization.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Rational ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But I've been doing my best to be rational as well. Even though I keep reading and practicing information analysis ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I ... can't make a choice. What if I make a wrong choice? What if there's no right answer? What if I never told Kakania about ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Enough. You're getting carried away.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: There is nothing mysterious about rationality. It simply guides us out of confusion and straight to the essence of things.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The essence?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The reason why we're doing a job here is simple, Marcus.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Arcanists keep going to the Manus. It's because they can promise the "salvation," while we can't.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Therefore, decoding their immunity ritual against the "Storm" is top priority. If we can't, being isolated on a small piece of land, we're bound to meet our end in this temporal catastrophe.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: We are not the only investigators sent by the headquarters. So our mission is to collect every clue left by the Manus and send them back to Laplace.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Everything else is secondary.
Marcus presses her lips tightly, not wanting to speak.
She takes a deep breath, following Hofmann's words as they step out of the darkness.
She can do nothing more than focus intently on their current situation.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Madam Hofmann, besides finding Ms. Kakania, there may be another way.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: That painting, the last work of Theophil, The Salvation. Something's off with it.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: When I read it in the exhibition, I felt a familiar afflatus. It was concealed in a clever way, but I noticed the traces of concealment.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Manus's arcane skill?
Marcus hesitates for a moment, performing at once a nod and shaking her head, creating a muddled response.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But I couldn't read anything more from it. If we can persuade Ms. Kakania to help us with her arcane skill ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Is her arcane skill similar to yours?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: No, quite different. I fought her once. I feel that under certain conditions, our arcane skills might be complementary.
Marcus posits wholeheartedly, once again drifting into her own thoughts.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Well done, Marcus. This is something only you can do.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The government has the painting now. The Field Agent Squad can retrieve it for us.
Hofmann nods, loading more bullets into the chamber.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The fog is cleared. Let's go.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Now, we need to find Kakania.
TO BE CONTINUED…
